translated_text: Pforzheim, May 26, 1933. Today is Friday, and I've already gotten a lot done at home again. But the work was very pleasant, as I mainly made objects. By the way, Dad also came back from Italy on Wednesday and, like me, brought new ideas. So, there's still a lot for me to do, but also to do alone. I'll probably have to stay here for a few more days. My journey was very pleasant, my dear. That is to say, I was all alone and slept wonderfully until five in the morning. It's funny, by the way. The athletes who boarded the train with me in Paris. Football players who played against the French national team, including some from Pforzheim, who won. Of course, in Strasbourg, they didn't question or search me this time. But I think I'll soon realize there's something about me that attracts people. If the compartment is full of people, he certainly won't search anyone but me. I'll talk to Dad about Paris in detail today and give him a report. I hope he'll be satisfied. I haven't heard from Zubi since then. Yes, we'll write to him today anyway. Father returned from Italy with relatively good results. The question now is how the representative will continue working with Ernst alone. The same applies to Zubi, of course. Walter Katz had to postpone his vacation and will only join us later. The matter with Indembing is still up in the air, but work is being done on it diligently. I'm sure of Zabalein that I'm not lacking in work, and that's how it is. I'm actually not tired at all and completely refreshed. I think my work in Paris was due to the constant back and forth. However, despite the risk of becoming somewhat tired again, I will try to come back to Paris as soon as possible. After being there twice in a row, it has almost become a matter of course for me that this will continue. Perhaps that's not a good thing; I don't know. But Paris hasn't become any more distant for me today than Frankfurt or Stuttgart. Perhaps also because I feel so comfortable with you, for which I am always very, very grateful. Your dear mother will soon receive a letter from me. Eat one while, and the self-gift as always. Your love to Mady Zweigenthal, Pforzheim, German Reich. Elisabeth Aigner, Paris 15e 7, 7 Jean Rue Nat Sicanol, PA C 30 18/0
